blocks.text: Now the README's Copilot paragraph:

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing PAT
— the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. CI runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Models come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","path":"README.md"}

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. | Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

messages.preview: Now the README's Copilot paragraph:

blocks.text: Now the README's Copilot paragraph:

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing PAT
— the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. CI runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Models come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","path":"README.md"}

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.

    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

## GitHub Copilot credentials

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. No 401 refresh-retry (nothing to refresh). Requires the token's **"Copilot Requests"** permission and a Copilot seat |
| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config

  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.

    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels

      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |

| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the

default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved

# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:

  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.

    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted

blocks.text: Now the README's Copilot paragraph:

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a

  required: true
  branch_coverage: true

  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.

    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known

    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.

  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid

  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the

  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.

    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)

  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

## GitHub Copilot credentials

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. No 401 refresh-retry (nothing to refresh). Requires the token's **"Copilot Requests"** permission and a Copilot seat |
| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

Headless flows: `--provider copilot --model <id>` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (OAuth or fine-grained PAT), or a saved entry's key slot (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`). `/provider export` copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (picker on several accounts; the token never prints to the transcript).","oldText":"| `openrouter` | env `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`); OAuth PKCE via `lib/src/providers/openrouter_oauth.dart` + `services/openrouter_oauth_*` | `api: 'openai-completions'`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `/api/v1/models` |","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing PAT
— the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. CI runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Models come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","path":"README.md"}

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

## GitHub Copilot credentials

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. No 401 refresh-retry (nothing to refresh). Requires the token's **"Copilot Requests"** permission and a Copilot seat |
| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

Headless flows: `--provider copilot --model <id>` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (OAuth or fine-grained PAT), or a saved entry's key slot (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`). `/provider export` copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (picker on several accounts; the token never prints to the transcript).","oldText":"| `openrouter` | env `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`); OAuth PKCE via `lib/src/providers/openrouter_oauth.dart` + `services/openrouter_oauth_*` | `api: 'openai-completions'`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `/api/v1/models` |","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing PAT
— the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. CI runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

## GitHub Copilot credentials

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. No 401 refresh-retry (nothing to refresh). Requires the token's **"Copilot Requests"** permission and a Copilot seat |
| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

Headless flows: `--provider copilot --model <id>` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (OAuth or fine-grained PAT), or a saved entry's key slot (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`). `/provider export` copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (picker on several accounts; the token never prints to the transcript).","oldText":"| `openrouter` | env `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`); OAuth PKCE via `lib/src/providers/openrouter_oauth.dart` + `services/openrouter_oauth_*` | `api: 'openai-completions'`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `/api/v1/models` |","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing PAT
— the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. CI runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

## GitHub Copilot credentials

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. No 401 refresh-retry (nothing to refresh). Requires the token's **"Copilot Requests"** permission and a Copilot seat |
| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

Headless flows: `--provider copilot --model <id>` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (OAuth or fine-grained PAT), or a saved entry's key slot (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`). `/provider export` copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (picker on several accounts; the token never prints to the transcript).","oldText":"| `openrouter` | env `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`); OAuth PKCE via `lib/src/providers/openrouter_oauth.dart` + `services/openrouter_oauth_*` | `api: 'openai-completions'`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `/api/v1/models` |","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}

blocks.text: Now the README's Copilot paragraph:

{"newText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
for a short-lived Copilot API token; a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`,
needs the "Copilot Requests" permission) is used directly against the
Copilot API — no exchange, so it works anywhere a stable revocable
credential matters (docker/CI). Classic `ghp_` tokens are not supported
by Copilot. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. `/provider export` copies the saved
account's token to the clipboard (for moving it to a headless box). CI
runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (an OAuth token or a fine-grained PAT). Models
come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a
custom client id carries an account-ban risk; override only with cause.","oldText":"GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing PAT
— the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Accounts save as named entries (`copilot-<login>` by
default); the plan picks the host — individual `api.githubcopilot.com`,
business `api.business.githubcopilot.com`, enterprise
`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`, or a custom `--base-url` override —
and several accounts can coexist side by side. Tokens live only in the
OS secure store (Keychain / Secret Service); `config.yaml` carries name,
plan, and baseUrl, never a token. CI runs store-less via the
`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env (plus a `_2`… ring for more entries), and
headless runs take `--provider copilot --model <id>` with
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Models come from a live `GET /models` (with
capabilities and limits). The device-flow client id is overridable via
`FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` — that GitHub endpoint is undocumented, so a

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: the whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was stage_size +
  # ci.yml shell find-exec, gh-1232). wc -l semantics, generated output
  # excluded — nothing exceeds 2800 today, so the shrink-only baseline
  # starts EMPTY of loc entries. Scope = the package sources [lib, bin]:
  # 0.11.0 has NO per-gate sources override (gates.loc.sources is a
  # ConfigException — caught by CI on 019ede65), and the top-level
  # sources drive the CRAP census too, so they stay untouched. test/ and
  # example/ are enforced by the companion config
  # crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml (same loc gate, sources [test, example]);
  # the app package's own config covers flutter_app/lib.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - '**.g.dart'
      - '**.freezed.dart'
      - '**.mocks.dart'
      - 'vendor/**'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false} # follow-up card (issue #1234 §5). Known
    # FPs to exclude when enabling: the conditional-export IO entry points
    # (lib/io.dart, lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart — public barrels whose
    # importers live outside this repo's import graph) and shared pinned
    # data modules imported only from test/ (lib/src/cli/omp_reg_scenarios.dart,
    # issue #810). lib/fanet.dart was the one confirmed-dead hit — deleted
    # in #1234.
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

## GitHub Copilot credentials

Three supported GitHub credential shapes (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart`):

| Credential | Support |
| --- | --- |
| Device-flow OAuth token (`gho_`/`ghu_`) | **Recommended.** `/provider copilot` → GitHub device flow; exchanged for a ~30-min Copilot API token (single-flight, proactive refresh 2 min before expiry, one 401/403 refresh+retry) |
| `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (headless) | An OAuth token (exchanged like above) **or** a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) |
| Fine-grained PAT (pasted or env) | **PAT mode:** the exchange is skipped entirely — the raw PAT is the Bearer against the configured base URL (the seat's tier host), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`) — the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with. No 401 refresh-retry (nothing to refresh). Requires the token's **"Copilot Requests"** permission and a Copilot seat |
| Classic PAT (`ghp_…`) | Never supported by Copilot — rejected at paste time |

Headless flows: `--provider copilot --model <id>` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (OAuth or fine-grained PAT), or a saved entry's key slot (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`). `/provider export` copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (picker on several accounts; the token never prints to the transcript).","oldText":"| `openrouter` | env `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`); OAuth PKCE via `lib/src/providers/openrouter_oauth.dart` + `services/openrouter_oauth_*` | `api: 'openai-completions'`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `/api/v1/models` |","path":"docs/agents/providers.md"}
